transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been really stuck on how my face looks. Mostly the left side—it looks uneven and kind of puffy to me, especially on video calls or in salsa photos. Other people say they don’t notice it, but I can’t seem to let it go, and it’s starting to affect work and going out.
Is it only your face, particularly the left side, that you're concerned about, or are there other parts of your body that you also worry about?

It’s mostly my face… the left side, really. I keep seeing it as uneven or puffy, especially on video calls or in photos from salsa. People say they don’t notice anything, but I still get stuck on it. It’s been affecting work and going out.
Have your concerns about your face's appearance changed over time or have they remained the same?

It’s mostly stayed the same, I think. I keep coming back to the left side of my face looking uneven or puffy… especially on video calls or in dance photos. Even when people say they don’t see it, I still focus on it, and it’s been getting in the way a bit with work and going out.
How much distress does thinking about the left side of your face cause you on a daily basis?

It’s… pretty upsetting most days. I try not to think about it, but then I’ll see myself on a video call or a salsa photo and I get stuck on how uneven and puffy that side looks. Even when people say they don’t see it, it still bothers me enough that it affects work and going out sometimes.
Do you ever have days where you're less concerned about the left side of your face after someone tells you it looks fine?

Maybe for a little bit, yeah. If someone says it looks fine, I can calm down briefly… but then I’ll see myself on a video call or in a salsa photo and I’m right back to focusing on the left side looking uneven or puffy. It’s hard to shake, even when people say they don’t see it.
Has your concern about the left side of your face ever caused you to avoid social interactions or work-related activities altogether?

Yeah… I have. Not all the time, but enough that it’s been a problem.

I’ve joined some video calls late because I couldn’t get past how I looked, and I’ve missed ticket deadlines at work. My supervisor actually brought it up in a performance review, which was… embarrassing.

And socially, I’ve skipped salsa nights or community events if I knew people would probably be taking photos.
Do you think you would still be concerned about your appearance if the left side of your face looked perfectly even and not puffy to you?

I don’t know… maybe I’d find something else, but right now it’s really that left side. The unevenness, the puffiness—especially on video calls or salsa photos. I can’t seem to stop checking it, even when people say they don’t notice anything.
Have you ever found yourself worrying about how another part of your body looks, not just your face?

Not really… it’s mostly my face. The left side, specifically. I keep noticing it looking uneven or puffy, especially on video calls or in salsa photos, even when people tell me they don’t see anything.
Do you think your concern about your face could ever shift to something else, like your hair or body shape, if the left side of your face no longer bothered you?

I’m not sure. I mean… maybe, but I haven’t really noticed that happening.

Right now it’s just my face—mostly the left side looking uneven or puffy. That’s what I keep getting stuck on, especially with video calls or photos.
Do you think you could ever become concerned about a different part of your face, not just the left side?

Maybe… I don’t really know. Right now I’m just stuck on the left side looking uneven or puffy, especially when I see myself on video calls or in salsa photos. People say they don’t see it, but I keep focusing on it anyway.
Do you think you could become concerned about another part of your face if the left side no longer bothered you?

I don’t really know. I guess it’s possible, but I can’t picture it right now.

What I’m stuck on is the left side looking uneven or puffy—like on video calls or in salsa photos. Even when people say they don’t see it, I keep focusing on it, and it’s been affecting work and going out.
Is your concern only about how you look, or are you also worried about other things being imperfect or not just right?

Mostly just how I look, I think. It’s… the left side of my face looking uneven or puffy, especially on video calls or in photos from salsa. People say they don’t notice it, but I keep seeing it, and it’s been getting in the way of work and going out.
Are you worried about being imperfect in areas of your life beyond your appearance?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think about it that way much… it mostly feels tied to how I look.
Are there areas in your life, outside of how you look, where you feel the need for everything to be perfect?
Not really… I mean, I like to do things well, but I don’t think I need everything to be perfect outside of my appearance. At least, nothing that stands out to me.
Are there any areas in your life where you feel like things need to be just right, beyond how you look?
No… not really. I can’t think of anything like that. It’s mostly just the appearance stuff.
Is there anything else in your life, besides how you look, that you feel is significantly affecting your daily life or causing you distress?
I don’t think so… not anything major. It’s mostly the way I look that gets to me.
Do you think your concern about the left side of your face could completely go away if you were convinced it looked perfectly normal?

I… I think so, maybe. If I could really believe the left side of my face looked normal, I don’t think I’d be so stuck on it. That’s kind of why I came in — I keep noticing it on video calls or in salsa photos, like it looks uneven or puffy, even when people say they don’t see it. It’s been getting in the way more than I want to admit.
Is there anything in your life, besides how you look, that you feel is significantly imperfect or bothers you?
No… I don’t think so. Nothing really comes to mind besides the face thing.
